items.rawSummary: Senator Lindsey Graham died at Walter Reed National Military Medical Center, prompting Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu to plan a U.S. visit for his memorial and a potential meeting with President Trump, as the administration intensifies military and economic pressure on Iran.
items.analysis: Senator Graham passed away at Walter Reed, prompting Netanyahu to call it a great loss for Israel. After the White House had previously indicated no visit was on Trump's schedule, Israeli officials now confirm Netanyahu will fly to the U.S. on Saturday and is expected to attend the memorial in Washington next Tuesday; his office is seeking a meeting with Trump during the trip. The death and diplomatic movements unfold as the administration intensifies military planning on Iran: President Trump held a Situation Room meeting to discuss broader strikes deeper inside the country beyond the current Strait of Hormuz campaign, threatening to escalate in the coming days unless Iran negotiates over its nuclear program. The U.S. also expanded sanctions on Iran's oil sector, targeting the shipping network of petroleum magnate Mohammad Hossein Shamkhani and freezing $130 million in digital wallets linked to Iran's central bank, AFP reported, as airstrikes and a naval blockade continue for a fourth straight day. The Pentagon's public war cost estimate of $30 billion contrasts with internal figures of $80–100 billion, while Defense Secretary Hegseth blocked the promotions of seven senior Navy officers—an action that means no active-duty female officer is likely to rise to admiral this year for the first time in over a decade. Meanwhile, Senate Democrats blocked debate on the $1.15 trillion defense bill, opposing the expansion of the war and provisions that deepen U.S.-Israel military cooperation.

items.title: Imam Khomeini Hussainiya, Tehran, Iran: Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said the US had terminated the lifting of Iran's naval blockade and completely dismantled the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding.
items.description: Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said the US had terminated the lifting of Iran's naval blockade and completely dismantled the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding.
items.rawSummary: Former President Ahmadinejad's appearance at the Imam Khomeini Hussainiya memorial countered allegations of his house arrest, while U.S.-Iran military tensions intensified with overnight airstrikes, infrastructural threats, and a reported Iranian cyber espionage campaign tracking U.S. forces.
items.analysis: Ahmadinejad's public appearance at the Imam Khomeini Hussainiya memorial, one day after an investigation alleged his house arrest, offered apparent counter-evidence even as U.S.-Iran military tensions surged. Overnight, CENTCOM confirmed a seven-hour operation destroying dozens of Iranian military sites near the Strait of Hormuz, with an Iranian Health Ministry official reporting over 260 wounded and the IRGC claiming retaliatory strikes on bases in Bahrain and Kuwait. President Trump threatened to target power plants and bridges next week unless Iran negotiates, while Deputy Foreign Minister Gharibabadi declared Iran would never request talks. Amid the confrontation, reports emerged that Iranian operatives conducted a cyber espionage campaign exploiting mobile networks and advertising data to track U.S. military personnel. The crisis compounds a severe economic downturn—the rial has lost over 99% of its value since 2002 and the minimum wage covers just 37% of subsistence costs—while in Tehran a coffin bearing Trump’s image was displayed and Iran executed a man convicted of arson during the 2026 protests.

items.title: Beijing, China, China: China's economy grew 4.3% year-on-year in Q2 (April–June), the weakest pace since late 2022, according to government data.
items.description: China's economy grew 4.3% year-on-year in Q2 (April–June), the weakest pace since late 2022, according to government data.
items.rawSummary: Beijing urged safe passage in the Strait of Hormuz, is recalibrating relations with Moscow, and faces domestic economic headwinds as second-quarter growth slowed to 4.3% year-on-year.
items.analysis: China's capital urged the United States and Iran to restore safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz and pledged to work to ease tensions, a call made amid concern over navigation in the critical oil transit chokepoint. The Wall Street Journal separately reported that Beijing is preparing for a Russia after Vladimir Putin, cultivating ties with other powerful figures in Moscow, and that the balance of power has shifted with China refusing to buy Russian gas except at below-market rates. US officials also said shipments of Nvidia H200 chips to China have begun, pushing Nvidia shares to a new intraday high and highlighting the flow of advanced semiconductors despite export controls. The government reported on Wednesday that the economy grew 4.3% year-on-year in the second quarter, the weakest pace since late 2022, adding domestic pressure to a picture of multifaceted international maneuvering.

items.title: Havana, Cuba: China's Foreign Ministry condemns the U.S. blockade of Cuba, says it has caused profound suffering, and voices support for Cuba's sovereignty and opposition to external interference.
items.description: China's Foreign Ministry condemns the U.S. blockade of Cuba, says it has caused profound suffering, and voices support for Cuba's sovereignty and opposition to external interference.
items.rawSummary: Cuba is enduring a severe energy crisis after its third nationwide blackout in ten days, while China condemned the long-standing U.S. embargo and voiced support for Cuban sovereignty.
items.analysis: Cuba's power grid collapsed for the third time in less than ten days, highlighting chronic generation failures and deepening humanitarian strain on the island. The repeated blackouts have underscored the fragility of the country's energy infrastructure. On July 15, China's Foreign Ministry publicly attributed the Cuban people's suffering to six decades of U.S. blockade and sanctions, calling for an immediate end to those measures and affirming China's backing of Cuba's right to national sovereignty and resistance to external interference. The statement adds a diplomatic dimension to the ongoing crisis.

items.title: Seoul, South Korea: Foreign investors sold a record $110 billion in South Korean equities year-to-date, with outflows more than doubling since early May and June alone seeing the largest monthly outflow in history at $31 billion.
items.description: Foreign investors sold a record $110 billion in South Korean equities year-to-date, with outflows more than doubling since early May and June alone seeing the largest monthly outflow in history at $31 billion.
items.rawSummary: South Korea deepens security and defense industry ties with NATO against a backdrop of North Korea’s confirmed artillery support to Russia and a record-breaking foreign investor exit from its stock market.
items.analysis: South Korea is deepening its engagement with NATO members and seeking a larger footprint in the international defense industry, a course it is pursuing even as North Korea explicitly condemns Seoul-NATO ties. The latest Ukrainian intelligence assessment adds concrete weight to Pyongyang’s antagonism: North Korea has supplied Russia with hundreds of artillery systems and now provides an estimated 25 to 40 percent of Russian artillery ammunition, linking the peninsula’s tensions directly to the war in Ukraine. Seoul’s ambition to diversify its security partnerships and defense exports beyond the immediate peninsula thus unfolds while North Korea’s military alignment with Moscow grows. Unrelated to the security landscape, South Korea’s equity market is under severe strain, with foreign investors selling a record $110 billion in equities year-to-date and June alone registering the largest monthly outflow ever, highlighting an accelerating financial headwind that could complicate the economic outlook.

items.description: Yemeni forces claim shooting down a Saudi Wing Loong 2 reconnaissance drone over Al-Bayda.
items.rawSummary: Houthi officials claimed that a Saudi reconnaissance drone was shot down over Al-Bayda, underscoring the persistent aerial dimension of Yemen's ongoing conflict.
items.analysis: A Houthi spokesperson claimed on July 14 that a Saudi Wing Loong 2 reconnaissance drone was shot down over Al-Bayda airspace while carrying out hostile missions. The statement echoes an earlier, near-identical announcement from a spokesperson for the Houthi-aligned Yemeni Armed Forces. These claims highlight the continual aerial activity and risk in Yemen's protracted war, though independent verification is unavailable. Saudi officials have not publicly responded to the reported downing.
